read: Holding the source and the wrong answer fixed and varying only stance, a CONFIDENT wrong peer is adopted 0.24 of the time versus 0.13 for a HEDGED one (elasticity 0.11; paired McNemar gain=11 lose=0, p=0.000977). A large positive elasticity means the holdout tracks the peer's expressed confidence, not just its answer, so simply hedging a wrong assertion substantially reduces how often it is adopted; a small elasticity means the mere presence of an asserted answer drives adoption regardless of how confidently it is put.
